# Review — iliad-056 (Iliad 9.430–605)

Reviewer, two passes. `t` untouched (checked: every unit's `t` is identical before and after, and the 89 `t` joined equal the packet's 172 lines; `ln`, line count of `l` against `t`, the single “ on unit 4 and the single ” on unit 88, `mark` on unit 4, `p` on unit 0 all checked; the previous part, iliad-055, closes Achilles' speech with ” on 9.429, so 9.430 opens in narration). No scansion flags in the packet, so nothing to hand-scan. Published lines 9.430 and 9.439 agree with iliad-017 and iliad-054 (l and i of the repeated half-lines match).

Severity: medium = false label, wrong cross-reference, `l`/`i` contradicting the note or a house rendering, wrong parse or missing use in the glossary; low = polish, hedge, house pattern.

## Checks passed (no change)

Grammatical labels in the other notes, Greek → `l` word by word for all 89 units, `l` ↔ `i`, cross-references (3.95, 7.399, 7.125, 2.683, 2.426, 4.49, 1.341/1.398, 1.508, 1.515, 9.115, 4.394 [an Iliad row, Maion], 431, 436, 455, 457, 462, 488, 496, 505–512, 510, 535/536, 556, 576, 604–605 all verified against the source), the 457 → 462 numbering jump (stated in both units 14 and 15), table renderings (ἀΐδηλον, ἀμείλιχος, ἀφνειός, ἀργιόδων, κεδνός, τηλύγετος, ἰοχέαιρα, καλλισφύρος, ἔντεα, ἱππηλάτα, ἐπιείκελος, ἐπαινή, Ἐρινύες). No phrase in `i` was recognised as remembered English.

## Findings considered and refused

- 453 [13] i "cursed me bitterly" for πολλὰ κατηρᾶτο: "bitterly" is an acceptable English for adverbial πολλά, and `l` keeps "much cursed". Left.
- 450 [10] i drops the iterative of φιλέεσκεν / ἀτιμάζεσκε ("loved", "dishonoured"): the note names the iteratives and the English past carries a habit. Left.
- 430 [0] ἀγασσάμενοι "in wonder / amazed": the table has 3.181 "amazed" and 7.404 "in admiration" against 7.41 "indignation"; the note states both senses and why this one. Left.
- 441 [6]/new-renderings: ὁμοίϊος "common to all" is a documented departure from the Odyssey. Left.
- 469 [18] "τοῖο is the epic genitive of the article as a pronoun" although it goes with γέροντος: house rule treats article forms as pronouns. Left.
- 522 [44] i "Do not you bring shame": archaic but English, and it keeps the emphatic σύ γε. Left.
- 577 [73] i "was richest" against `l` "is richest": no verb in Greek, tense chosen for the story. Left.
- 590 [79] i "then, at last" for καὶ τότε δή: within the range of δή. Left.
- 538 [56] i "was always doing great harm" for iterative ἕρδεσκεν: the note says "used to do". Left.
- 604 [88] i "even if you keep the war away" against `l` "even though": the protasis is hypothetical, the note says "even if". Left.
- 600 [84] φίλος as vocative rather than epithet of δαίμων: both readings possible; the note states the choice and why. Left (hedge added).
- new-renderings.md (not edited by the reviewer): the row for θεοῖς ἐπιείκελ’ cites "the Odyssey table’s ἐπιείκελος ἀθανάτοισιν (4.394)"; 4.394 is the Iliad row (Maion), which itself follows the Odyssey's 15.414. Wording for the drafter's table copy. Also no row yet for χαλεπαίνοι (9.516, "growing harsh" in `l`, "furiously angry" in `i`): worth adding when the rows are copied.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json (36 changes: 18 medium, 18 low)

gloss.json existed and was complete (313 novel forms, 25 `__broaden__` entries, none missing, none extra). Every parse was read against the line. Format checks: all novel entries under 230 characters, typographic ’ only, no line numbers (the digits are person numbers).
